data.title: US STOCKS-Nasdaq futures slide as Anthropic retreat deepens AI jitters
data.description:
* Futures down: Dow 0.1%, S&P 500 0.74%, Nasdaq 1.64%

* Anthropic down 7.4% a day after debut

* Intuit down after company cuts revenue forecast, agrees to sell unit

(Updates prices throughout, adds analyst comment)

By Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur

Nov 20 (Reuters) - Nasdaq futures fell more than 1% on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the high-profile listing would stabilize an AI trade already shaken by valuation concerns, while hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment.

Anthropic shares slid 7.4% in premarket trading after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut. The stock began trading more than 34% above its offer price of $83.

Anthropic's IPO and Nvidia's ( NVDA ) earnings this week were seen as key tests of whether battered investor confidence in the AI trade could recover.

But neither revived enthusiasm after weeks of concern about the profitability of massive AI infrastructure spending, rising borrowing costs, regulatory risks following Democrats' win in the US midterm elections, and Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's departure.

"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."

As of Thursday's close, the Nasdaq was 13.6% below its October 6 record closing high, while the S&P 500 had posted its sixth consecutive loss, its longest losing streak since April 2024.

The main US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon ( AMZN ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) declined more than 1.5% each, while Meta fell 2% and Alphabet was muted. Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) fell 2.2%, while Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), Marvell ( MRVL ), and Micron lost between 2.2% and 6.6%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also dropped about 5% each.

Data center stocks IREN ( IREN ), Applied Digital ( APLD ) and Core Scientific ( CORZ ) fell about 4% each.

At 7:03 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were down 48 points, or 0.1%, and S&P 500 E-minis were down 53.5 points, or 0.74%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 436 points, or 1.64%.

The CBOE Volatility Index, Wall Street's fear gauge, hit the 30-point mark for the first time since March 30.

The selloff in AI-linked stocks has largely overshadowed a strong earnings season.

Of the 462 companies in the S&P 500 to have reported results through Wednesday, 83.5% beat analyst earnings expectations, according to an analysis from Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

Markets are pricing in a 98.4% chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 9.7% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

(Reporting by Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel)

data.title: Analysis-Trump touts Asia trade deal wins, but US agricultural exports disappoint
data.description:
CHICAGO, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump visited Asia this week, boasting of a string of agricultural trade victories since threatening to impose tariffs that would decimate other countries' trade.

US trade agreements have at times buoyed prices of crops and livestock, but a Reuters analysis of 10 deals showed few have generated a promised windfall of US farm product sales.

China, the largest US trading partner in Asia, appears on track to meet its commitment to buy 25 million metric tons of US soybeans in 2026, but purchases remain below levels seen before Trump's "Liberation Day" tariffs in April 2025. Beijing's agreement to buy $17 billion worth of other US farm products this year is largely unfulfilled.

The data undercuts White House messaging that Trump's trade tactics are benefiting US farmers and ushering in what the president has called a "golden age" of agriculture. Dissatisfaction over the president's tariff strategy contributed to losses for Trump's Republican Party in this month's midterm elections, including among farmers who voted for Trump, analysts say.

The Trump administration says it has secured around a dozen trade deals with Asian countries since imposing tariffs, easing plant and livestock health requirements for incoming US products and expanding low-tariff import quotas. Some included minimum annual purchase commitments for US crops and meat.

But agricultural exports to partner nations often increased immediately following White House announcements before tapering off, the Reuters analysis found.

"The reality is that this has been a lot of talk and not much action," said Scott Lincicome, vice president of economics and trade at the Cato Institute think tank.

During Trump's Asia trip this week, he said the US reached a "very big trade deal" with the Philippines. Manila said, however, the two countries had reached an understanding on economic cooperation.

MISSED TARGETS

Some deals have been finalized, but have not met their targets.

Indonesia, the 12th-largest US agricultural products importer by value, agreed in February to import $4.5 billion of farm goods. But in the first nine months of 2026, US exports totaled less than $2.4 billion, roughly in line with the same period over the last decade, according to US Census Bureau trade data.

Indonesia agreed to import 3.5 million tons of US soybeans annually, but just 54% of that goal had shipped as of September, the trade data showed. Wheat exports of less than 450,000 tons represented less than a quarter of Indonesia's annual commitment, while soymeal exports of just 150,000 tons made up 4% of a 3.8-million-ton target.

The White House said a trade agreement with Malaysia, signed in October 2025, would provide US exporters "unprecedented access" to its market. The deal promised to open market access for US sorghum and facilitate pork and poultry exports. However, 2026 US pork exports through September were down 52% from the same period a year earlier, while there were zero poultry and sorghum shipments, US government data showed.

The text of a February trade deal with Bangladesh, following Trump's threat of tariffs that could devastate the South Asian nation's textiles industry, stated that the country or companies there would buy at least 700,000 tons of US wheat annually for five years and $1.25 billion worth or 2.6 million tons of soy and soy products over one year. Since then, US wheat exports totaled 473,000 tons while combined soybean and soymeal shipments reached just 162,000 tons, US government data showed.

Trade talks with China have shown mixed results. Trump met on Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen after a brief stop in the Philippines for a Southeast Asian summit.

The world's top soybean importer halted purchases from the US last year as the trade war heated up, but resumed modest purchases after talks in Busan, South Korea, last October and in Beijing in May. But China has not lifted its 10% tariff on US soybeans, so government buyers booked the nearly 20 million tons from the current US harvest. Private Chinese importers continued to buy from rival supplier Brazil.

The White House said it secured a deal for Beijing to buy $17 billion of other US agricultural goods annually, with this year's target prorated. But the US has exported less than $2.5 billion of US farm goods, excluding soybeans, to China since the May summit through September, US government data showed.

In a statement, the White House said China has achieved "partial compliance" with its Busan agreement, but did not respond to detailed questions about other Asian trading partners. The Office of the US Trade Representative did not have immediate comment.

Trump's trade approach has damaged the country's reputation as a reliable trading partner, according to analysts and exporters, and spurred traditional trading partners to strike deals with rival exporters.

"Everybody else in the world is like, 'We are not going to follow Trump off the tariff cliff. We're not going to really retaliate against the United States, but we'll retaliate indirectly by lowering our barriers to everybody else'," Lincicome said.

(Reporting by Karl Plume in Chicago. Editing by Emily Schmall and Rod Nickel)

data.title: Cytta Air Expands Military Contracting Expertise - Appoints Rear Admiral James "Gib" Godwin III to Advisory Board
data.description:
LAS VEGAS, NM / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Cytta Corp. ( CYCA ) and its technology spin-out, Cytta Air Corp. today announced the appointment of Rear Admiral James Basil "Gib" Godwin III, U.S. Navy (Retired), to their Advisory Board. Admiral Godwin brings extensive experience in aviation, technology acquisition, systems integration and program execution as Cytta Air advances its U.S.-made drone ecosystem and real-time intelligence platforms.

During his 33-year Navy career, Admiral Godwin held senior leadership roles spanning aircraft development, production and enterprise information systems. As Program Executive Officer for Tactical Aircraft, he oversaw approximately $5.5 billion in annual budgets across eight major acquisition programs, including delivery of the F/A-18 E/F Super Hornet for its first combat deployment. He subsequently served as the Navy's first Program Executive Officer for Enterprise Information Systems, managing IT services expenditures exceeding $1.4 billion annually.

Admiral Godwin's experience connects two central elements of Cytta Air's business: aircraft platforms and the secure information systems that turn live data into useful operational intelligence. As a Senior Advisor, Godwin will provide strategic guidance on government engagement, technology integration and the transition from product development to production and adoption.

"Gib understands what it takes to move complex technology from development into reliable, operational use," said Natalia Sokolova, President and COO of Cytta Air. "His experience in aviation, secure information systems and acquisition will help us align our products with customer requirements and build the relationships needed to bring affordable American-made drones and real-time intelligence to both the military and civilian users."

Following his Navy service, Godwin held leadership positions at one of the top four major U.S. defense contractors and PricewaterhouseCoopers. He founded BriteWerx, Inc., a service-disabled veteran-owned consulting business focused on aerospace, information technology, cybersecurity and emerging technologies. A decorated naval aviator, he accumulated more than 4,500 flight hours and holds a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering from Tulane University.

About Cytta Air Corp

Cytta Air is developing an affordable, secure, U.S.-made drone ecosystem built around proprietary drone designs, domestic manufacturing and real-time intelligence. Its patrol drones pair with IGAN™-Incident Global Area Network-a device-agnostic live video streaming and collaboration platform that connects drones, cameras and response teams to support public safety and critical infrastructure protection.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks slide as AI selloff deepens, Asia has worst week since 2020
data.description:
* Asian stocks on track for worst week since COVID hit

* Anthropic's historic debut fails to revive faith in AI trade

* US futures fall after S&P 500 drops for six straight sessions

(Updates prices, adds comment and chart)

By Harry Robertson, Jiaxing Li and Rae Wee

LONDON/HONG KONG/SINGAPORE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Stock markets stumbled around the world on Friday after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore investors' faith in the AI sector, with US futures dropping and Asian shares heading for their worst week since 2020.

Government bonds rallied as investors sought safe-haven assets.

Shares of Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, jumped as it launched the biggest IPO in history on Thursday, although they pared gains later in the session and were down 10% in premarket trading on Friday.

The debut did little to revive excitement over the broader AI theme, however, as investors continued to question whether the huge amounts of spending would deliver returns.

"The Anthropic IPO gave us some brief respite from the cloud of negativity," said Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar. "That pause is well and truly over unfortunately."

Futures for the tech-focused Nasdaq 100 fell 2% after the index dropped the same amount on Thursday. The Nasdaq is now down around 15% since hitting a record high in early October.

S&P 500 futures were in the red after the index fell for a sixth straight session on Thursday. A seven-day run of declines would be the worst streak since the pandemic.

The STOXX 600 gauge of European stocks fell almost 2%, while MSCI's world index of stocks fell for a seventh straight session , its longest losing streak since 2023.

The MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan tumbled and has sunk 8% this week, its worst performance since the COVID pandemic in March 2020.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) blowout earnings earlier in the week and Anthropic's IPO have both failed to restore confidence, said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at bank and investment firm Saxo.

"The market is no longer looking for proof of AI demand alone," she said. "It wants evidence that the extraordinary spending across the ecosystem can generate sustainable returns."

The VIX index of expected volatility on Wall Street stocks jumped and traded at its highest since March on Friday.

Adding to the unease, a report on AMD from a media outlet associated with short-selling fund Hunterbrook Capital raised concerns that the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some linked to blacklisted firms, could draw greater US regulatory scrutiny to the sector.

"No one headline drove the roll, though some pointed to an AMD short report which tapered overall sentiment," said Goldman Sachs analysts in a trading note.

All of that has piled further pressure on the AI trade, already battered in recent weeks by Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia ( NVDA ) and growing anti-data-centre sentiment exemplified by the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 5%. Taiwanese shares were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990.

Despite the sharp drop in stocks, however, equity markets remain up for the year after a blistering rally in the first half on AI optimism.

TREASURIES RALLY AS INVESTORS TAKE COVER

US Treasuries rallied as stocks took a beating, sending investors towards assets deemed safe havens.

The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes fell for a fifth straight session, to below 5%, while German 10-year bond yields fell 10 bps, the most since April . Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Meanwhile, the US dollar held steady at around its highest level in 20 months, also garnering support from growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in.

Oil prices were steady, with Brent crude futures trading at $90 a barrel and on track for a third week of declines.

(Reporting by Harry Robertson in London, Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong and Rae Wee in Singapore; Editing by Lincoln Feast, Xevi Fontdegloria and Mark Potter)

data.title: Consortium of Advent, FedEx, A&R and PPF Completes Acquisition of InPost
data.description:
• InPost completes its transition to private ownership, backed by a Consortium committed to accelerating its growth as a leading European consumer-centric e-commerce enabler.
  • InPost remains operationally independent and headquartered in Poland, led by CEO and founder Rafał Brzoska and the existing management team.
  • Advent, FedEx ( FDX ), A&R and PPF bring together long-term capital, deep sector knowledge, complementary commercial expertise and broad industry networks to help drive InPost’s future growth across Europe.
  • The Consortium will accelerate investment in InPost’s pan-European out-of-home network, underpinned by continued innovation in its technology platform and consumer proposition.
  • InPost’s growth strategy will be supported by arm’s length commercial agreements connecting InPost’s B2C last-mile capabilities to FedEx’s global network of c.3 million businesses and 225 million recipients.
  • The transaction will seek to deliver tangible benefits across InPost’s growing network, from stronger delivery infrastructure for merchants and greater convenience for consumers across Poland and Western Europe to continued career growth opportunities for employees.

AMSTERDAM & LUXEMBOURG--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Funds managed and/or advised by Advent International, L.P. and/or its affiliates (“Advent”), FCWB LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of FedEx Corporation ( FDX ) (“FedEx”), A&R Investments Ltd. (“A&R”) and PPF Group (“PPF”), together forming the Consortium, today announce the completion of the acquisition of InPost S.A. (“InPost” or the “Company”). InPost is now wholly-owned by the Consortium and has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam.

A new chapter for InPost

data.title: Erasca Reports 44% Response Rate for ERAS-0015 in Advanced Pancreatic Cancer
data.description:
07:38 AM EST, 11/20/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Erasca ( ERAS ) reported positive updated phase 1 data for its pan-RAS drug ERAS-0015, with confirmed objective response rates, or ORR, of 44% in KRAS G12X pancreatic cancer and 60% in non-small cell lung cancer at 32 mg once daily, the company said Friday.

In pancreatic cancer, the confirmed ORR was 69% among patients with KRAS G12D or G12V mutations, with the drug remaining generally well tolerated and no dose discontinuations at 32 mg once daily, the company said.

Early combination data with chemotherapy, pembrolizumab and panitumumab supported further development, while ERAS-4001 showed encouraging preliminary phase 1 activity.

Erasca ( ERAS ) also reported a 75% response rate among four patients with bile duct cancer. However, the small group sizes mean the results are preliminary and will need confirmation in larger studies, it said.

The company plans to start a potentially registration-enabling trial in second-line lung cancer and a phase 3 first-line pancreatic cancer trial in H1 2027, it added.

Erasca ( ERAS ) shares were down 10% in premarket activity.

data.title: GRAPHIC-US equity funds draw inflows for a third straight week
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Investors bought US equity funds for a third straight week in the week to November 18, supported by strong earnings fundamentals and cooling crude oil prices despite a recent surge in market volatility and growing uncertainty over the AI trade.

They bought US equity funds of a net $45.71 billion, registering their largest weekly net purchase since September 23, LSEG Lipper data showed.

Fund investors remained optimistic about strong third-quarter earnings despite concerns about the AI trade. Heavy spending and expectations of tighter oversight and slower data-center expansion after Democrats' midterm sweep pressured technology stocks.

With about 94% of US large- and mid-cap companies having reported so far, earnings rose 40.2% from a year earlier, while the technology sector posted 65% growth, according to LSEG data covering 1,921 companies.

"We do not think that the economic expansion, corporate earnings cycle, or structural AI investment story has broken," Mark Haefele, chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management said in a note.

"Our base case for 2027 remains for economic growth close to trend, rising corporate profits, further growth in AI investment, and moderating inflation later in the year."

US large-cap funds attracted $31.7 billion during the week, their largest inflow in eight weeks. In contrast, mid-cap and small-cap funds recorded outflows of $1.15 billion and $535 million, respectively.

Among sectoral funds, technology funds attracted $10.3 billion, their largest inflow since June 16. Industrial and financial sector funds, meanwhile, saw notable outflows of $1.23 billion and $884 million, respectively.

US bond funds recorded their first weekly outflow in four weeks, with investors withdrawing a net $5.58 billion.

Long-term US government and Treasury funds and high-yield funds saw outflows of $2.64 billion and $2.31 billion, respectively. In contrast, short- to intermediate-term government and Treasury funds attracted $1.27 billion, while loan participation funds received $859 million.

Meanwhile, money market funds saw $19.12 billion in withdrawals, marking a second consecutive weekly outflow.

(Reporting by Gaurav Dogra; Editing by Diti Pujara)

data.title: Fujifilm Expands ECHELON Synergy 1.5T MRI with ZeroHelium Technology and Dockable Patient Table Option
data.description:
New ZeroHelium MRI with advanced imaging, automation and flexibility helps healthcare providers speed exams with enhanced image quality and efficiency.

LEXINGTON, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- FUJIFILM Healthcare Americas Corporation, a leading provider of diagnostic and enterprise imaging solutions, announces the latest evolution of its ECHELON Synergy 1.5T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) platform. The new release expands customer choice with the availability of ECHELON Synergy ZeroHelium system, designed to operate without liquid helium while delivering high-quality imaging, intelligent workflow and patient-focused design. Fujifilm will showcase the new system for the first time in the U.S. at booth #4100 in South Hall at the 2026 Radiological Society of North America (RSNA) Conference & Annual Meeting held November 29 to December 2.

With the latest version 11 upgrades, healthcare organizations can configure ECHELON Synergy according to their clinical, operational and facility needs, including the option to select a ZeroHelium or conventional magnet, as well as options with or without the SynergyGlide dockable patient table. SynergyGlide is a power-assisted dockable table to enable patient preparation and transport outside of the exam room, to streamline workflow, patient handling and comfort.

“Healthcare providers are looking for MRI technology that can address not only clinical performance, but the operational realities of running a modern imaging department,” said Henry (Hidetoshi) Izawa, President and Chief Executive Officer, Global Head of Medical Informatics, FUJIFILM Healthcare Americas Corporation. “With ECHELON Synergy version 11, we’re giving customers greater flexibility to configure an MRI solution to meet their clinical and operational needs. ZeroHelium adds an important new option by helping reduce infrastructure requirements, while the platform’s advanced imaging and automation technologies are designed to help technologists work efficiently and deliver a positive patient experience.”

MRI Without Liquid Helium

Superconducting MRI systems have historically relied on liquid helium to cool their magnet coils and maintain superconductivity. Fujifilm’s ZeroHelium technology uses a dedicated cooling system to maintain superconductivity at approximately -269°C without requiring liquid helium, eliminating dependence on liquid helium while maintaining MRI operation. It can also help reduce risks associated with helium loss during unexpected events or power interruptions and provide more predictable operating costs.

Designed with thermal and mechanical factors in mind, the ZeroHelium magnet uses advanced engineering to control thermal effects and suppress vibration within the magnet, helping maintain consistent image quality. When an emergency ramp-down is not required, in-house staff can ramp down and restart the magnet in just a couple of hours instead of days without requiring a liquid helium refill, helping simplify recovery and reduce potential downtime.

Designed to Advance Imaging Quality and Productivity

Beyond its magnet technology, ECHELON Synergy version 11 incorporates advanced imaging and workflow capabilities designed to improve MRI efficiency. The system’s Deep Learning Reconstruction (DLR) technology helps reduce noise and enhance image clarity and can be applied to all body regions and a wide range of sequences. IP-RAPID is designed to help shorten scan times, and DLR Plus is designed to further refine image quality.

Workflow capabilities, including AutoExam, AutoPose and Auto Series, are designed to help reduce repetitive manual steps throughout exam setup and scanning by automatically performing exam and positioning steps. In the U.S., AutoExam is available for knee exams only, and AutoPose is available for anatomical regions other than the brain. AutoPose provides automated positioning across multiple anatomical regions, while Auto Series helps streamline scan sequencing and exam workflow, allowing technologists to spend more time focused on the patient.

ECHELON Synergy Version 11, including the ZeroHelium configuration, also features Synergy Vision, with monitoring cameras positioned at the front and rear of the bore to help operators monitor patient movement. The technology can identify movements that may contribute to artifacts, such as coughing or sneezing. Separate post-processing capabilities are designed to help reduce motion artifacts and potential repeat scans.

data.title: EMERGING MARKETS-EM equities eye biggest weekly drop since 2020 on AI rout, rate concerns
data.description:
* EM equities suffer worst week since 2020

* EM debt suffers biggest outflow since 2020

* Hungary's wage deal offers support to consumption

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Nov 20 (Reuters) - Emerging market stocks were on track for their biggest weekly drop since the COVID-19 pandemic selloff of 2020, as worries over a potential AI slowdown hammered tech-heavy Asian markets on Friday, while the prospects of higher US interest rates kept currencies under pressure.

Stocks in Taiwan plunged 6% to record their biggest weekly decline since 1990, while South Korea's Kospi fell more than 5% as investors unwound AI-linked bets across the globe despite a record-breaking debut for Anthropic and strong forecasts from chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ).

Tech stocks across the globe have sold off sharply in recent weeks as worries about tighter US regulation on data centre development and chip exports as well as the abrupt exit of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO fuelled concerns about the future of AI, especially after explosive growth in the technology boosted stock markets and economies this year.

MSCI's emerging market equities index fell 3%, on track to wipe out most of its year-to-date gains, in a sharp reversal from mid-June when it was up nearly 29%.

"The pillars of EM leadership are shifting. AI powered an exceptional 2026, but higher funding costs increasingly expose the ROIC-destructive economics of hyperscaler capex," Jefferies analysts said.

"A moderation in AI investment could trigger EM earnings downgrades, led by Korea and Taiwan, while India and China offer relative earnings resilience."

Indian stocks have been a rare bright spot, trading at nine-month highs, helped by a relative lack of exposure to AI companies and a sharp retreat in oil prices.

Equity markets in emerging Europe dropped too, with Poland's WIG20 down nearly 3% and Hungary's Budapest SE index falling 2.3%.

US RATE WORRIES

The MSCI EM currencies index dipped 0.1% and was set for its fourth consecutive weekly decline.

In South Africa, the rand hovered just below one-year lows against the dollar, on increasing bets on US interest rate hikes and the South African central bank's decision to keep interest rates unchanged. The currency steadied at 17.45 per dollar, having touched a one-year low of 17.56 earlier in the session.

Investor caution was also evident in debt markets, with Bank of America data showing EM debt funds recorded outflows of $7.5 billion in the latest week ending November 18, the largest withdrawal since April 2020.

In Hungary, meanwhile, the government said gross minimum wages would rise by 7.5% to 347,000 forints ($1,020.44) next year under an agreement reached late on Thursday with employers and trade unions, offering some support to domestic demand prospects.

The Hungarian forint weakened 0.3% against the euro, as investors awaited Moody's review of Hungary's sovereign rating later in the day.

The Polish zloty fell 0.4% amid fading hopes for a breakthrough in Ukraine. Polish authorities said they were investigating reports that at least two unidentified objects had fallen near the Ukrainian border after the military said the country's airspace may have been violated during Russian strikes on Ukraine.​‌

Investors were also keeping a close watch on developments in the Middle East.

Brent crude fell nearly 1% as robust crude exports from the Middle East eased supply concerns, overshadowing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.​‌

(Reporting by Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Sruthi Shankar in Bengaluru, Editing by Louise Heavens)

data.title: FOREX-Dollar set for fourth weekly gain, supported by Fed tightening expectations, AI-driven haven bid
data.description:
* Dollar index near strongest since early April 2025

* Markets debating size, not likelihood, of December Fed hike

* Yen firms after Japanese core inflation hits 2.2%

(Updates throughout)

By Sophie Kiderlin

LONDON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The dollar was steady on Friday and was on track to rise for the fourth straight week as expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening underpinned the US currency and jitters over the AI trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets.

The dollar index was perched near the 103.9 level, around its strongest since early April 2025. The weeks-long rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point hike in December should be considered.

The dollar was also supported by a reduced appetite for risk, with a multitude of AI-related concerns weighing on global stocks. Anthropic's record market debut on Thursday did little to revive investor confidence.

MSCI's world index of stocks fell for a seventh straight session on Friday, the longest losing streak since 2023.

Chris Turner, global head of markets at ING, said that while there is only a weak case for another steep correction in equities, "there is no reason for the Fed to drop its hawkish rhetoric anytime soon."

He pointed to next week's US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, a key inflation gauge for the Fed, which Turner said will likely confirm that the Fed needs to act.

"For FX, that means a continued strong dollar and continued pressure on popular carry trades," he said.

In FX carry trades, investors borrow in low-yielding currencies, such as the Japanese yen and Swiss franc, to fund purchases of higher-yielding assets elsewhere, often in emerging markets.

Adding to the hawkish-leaning narrative, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the evidence did not suggest inflation was heading back to 2% on its own.

"The debate now is not really about whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December, but how much it will raise rates by," Carol Kong, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said.

"We still think 25 basis points is more likely," Kong added. "If they really want to quicken the pace of tightening, I think they will prefer to increase rates by 25 bps in consecutive meetings rather than deliver a bigger-than-usual hike."

Sterling languished near a one-year low against the dollar at $1.3105, and the euro struggled near its lowest level since April 2025 and last bought $1.0961.

YEN FIRMS ON INFLATION DATA

The yen firmed 0.6% against the dollar to 158.78 and is set to close the week with a small gain after three weeks of losses that had dragged the currency to near the key 160 level.

Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that strengthen the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

Analysts at Capital Economics argue the yen's recent weakness is unlikely to last. With long-term inflation expectations now around target, further increases in yields would be mostly in real terms, which, combined with their view that US yields will fall, should prove yen-positive, the analysts said.

ING's Turner also noted that a carry trade unwind should be a slight positive for the yen.

(Reporting by Sophie Kiderlin in London, Li Gu in Shanghai and Rae Wee in Singapore; Editing by Tom Hogue, Sharon Singleton and Andrew Heavens)

data.title: Certainty for Every Token: Midea Debuts at SC26 with Modular Prefabricated Cooling Solutions to Accelerate AI Compute Deployment
data.description:
CHICAGO, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As AI computing demand surges, data center infrastructure is rapidly moving toward prefabrication and modular deployment. Beyond compute performance, getting capacity online faster has become a critical priority. However, the complex installation and commissioning of conventional cooling systems often become a bottleneck that slows down the entire build cycle. As the industry recognizes, an AI factory only creates value once it starts producing tokens, making plug-and-play cooling essential.

From November 17 to 19, Midea is showcasing at SC26 in Chicago, a leading North American event for HPC and AI infrastructure. Making its North American debut, Midea's modular prefabricated cooling solution features a core architecture of "Magnetic CDU + Dry cooler," delivering an integrated, cooling tower-free, all-climate solution for AI data centers.

From Standalone Equipment to Modular Prefabrication: Reshaping Cooling Delivery Efficiency

Conventional cooling systems rely on multiple standalone components, chillers, pumps, heat exchangers, and piping. This fragmented architecture complicates on-site installation and system integration, driving up engineering difficulty and time costs, and ultimately bottlenecking rapid compute deployment.

To address this, Midea integrates the cooling source, coolant distribution, and control into a single compact unit, forming a solution centered on the magnetic CDU and coordinated with dry coolers. Pre-assembled and pre-commissioned at the factory, the solution supports modular delivery for a true "plug-and-play" experience. In high-temperature regions, the compressor automatically engages to provide supplemental cooling, ensuring a stable supply liquid temperature of 20°C to 45°C for 8,760 hours a year. The solution has been deployed in batches at a large cloud provider's data center project in Southeast Asia, proving its performance in high-temperature and high-humidity environments.

From Cooling to Token: Enabling Faster Value Creation

Beyond the core architecture, Midea also offers a dry cooler container solution, co-developed with a leading U.S. customer, providing more modular and prefabricated options for varied climate, site, and load requirements.

As AI factories move toward prefabrication and rapid deployment, cooling efficiency has become a key factor in how quickly compute is put to use. Nov 20 (Reuters) - Every Friday, Reuters Open Interest (ROI) distills the financial week into five key charts, spotlighting the major trends, surprises and overlooked moves that defined the past five days.

1.SIZE MATTERS

MIKE DOLAN, ROI Finance & Markets Columnist: Anthropic's blockbuster IPO this week crowned a bumper year for US new listings in dollar terms, lifting 2026 IPO proceeds above the 2021 peak.

But as the year ​winds down, the actual number of IPOs in 2026 remains below last year's total and well below the average of the past decade. So while there is still a lot of capital available for new listings, the bar for making the cut has been raised. What this means for the future performance of the latest crop of mega caps remains to be seen.

2. CHIPPED ARMOR

JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: The Nvidia ( NVDA ) scandal has thrust a blinding spotlight on the US-China "AI arms race." Washington is tightening curbs on Chinese firms accessing advanced US chips, which Beijing still needs to keep its AI engine going.

For its part, Nvidia ( NVDA ) says it is effectively shut out of the Chinese market, although a Reuters review found more than $3 billion in Chinese computing projects used its restricted chips. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) share price is taking a hit, a beating that actually started well before CEO Jensen Huang resigned, shedding roughly $2 trillion of market cap in around six weeks.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stellar earnings report on Tuesday did little to stem the bleeding, especially given reports that the company is now the subject of a US Securities and Exchange Commission probe.

3. TAPS WIDE OPEN

RON BOUSSO, ROI Energy Columnist: Global benchmark Brent crude prices have fallen more than 20% since the start of the month, settling into a no-war, no-peace range just above $90 a barrel.

Gulf oil production and exports have risen steadily since August, easing pressure on global supplies, even as Middle East tensions have escalated, with multiple Iranian strikes on tankers in recent weeks. The poster child for this shaky new normal is Saudi Arabia. Its October oil output rose above its 2025 average despite continued attacks from Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militia on Saudi energy infrastructure.

4. GAME ON

ANNA SZYMANSKI, ROI Editor-in-Charge: Grand Theft Auto VI arrived on Thursday after a 13-year wait and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, making it one of the most anticipated video-game releases in history. It is expected to generate billions of dollars in first-week sales, delivering a major boost to the industry.

Its impact may extend beyond retail. Fans booked time off for marathon sessions, turning launch day into an unofficial holiday. Whether this leads to missed deadlines and angry bosses or simply a temporary, much-needed respite for stressed workers remains to be seen.

5. SHENZHEN REALITY CHECK

JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: US President Donald Trump has no shortage of economic troubles - inflation, rising interest rates and the Nvidia ( NVDA ) scandal, to name a few. But when he met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week, Xi may well have looked at Trump's hand with envy. China's domestic economy is still struggling with the fallout from the country's real estate bust, business investment is plummeting, and the stock market is down 20% since the summer. The only real bright spot is exports, boosted by tech and AI. But what if the AI bubble deflates?

data.title: France's EDF nears investment decision on new nuclear reactors, say sources
data.description:
* Utility targets December investment decision for six nuclear reactors

* Investment decision expected even without EU state aid approval

* EDF expected to auction of about 3,000 MW of electricity to reduce dominant market position

By Forrest Crellin

PARIS, Nov 20 (Reuters) - France's EDF plans to start hiring staff, placing orders and awarding contracts next year for six new nuclear reactors, even before securing final EU approval for a state-backed financing package, two sources familiar with the plans said.

The state-owned utility is pressing ahead with Europe's largest nuclear expansion project in decades, seeking to avoid the lengthy delays and ballooning costs that have plagued its past projects in France and Britain.

The programme to replace France's ageing reactors aims to bring a first reactor online by 2038 and is expected to cost more than €70 billion ($76.85 billion) for all six, with the government financing 60% through a zero-interest loan.

Under EU rules for state aid, the loan requires approval by the European Commission. But negotiations between Brussels and Paris are dragging on as the authority seeks assurance that the project will not give EDF greater market dominance.

EDF will in the meantime, however, take a provisional investment decision, the two people briefed on the plans said. That will allow it to begin ordering parts, hiring staff, awarding contracts and preparing construction sites to ensure the project sticks to its timeline.

"EDF wants to start fabricating the parts. People are already in place and ready to do that. We don't want to wait for that for one or two years," one of the people said.

French newspaper Les Echos reported earlier this week that EDF is discussing contracts worth €14 billion with builders Bouygues, Eiffage and Vinci.

EDF declined to comment on the contracts. It did not immediately respond to questions about the investment decision.

INVESTMENT DECISION SET FOR LATE DECEMBER

The nuclear expansion plan was developed at the outset of Russia's war in Ukraine, which caused a European energy crunch and coincided with an unexpected maintenance period that took half of France's reactors offline for checks and repairs.

It is intended to replace output from reactors approaching the end of their operating lives and help prevent a sharp decline in French nuclear generation from the middle of the century.

EDF's board is expected to review the investment decision in mid-December, finalise the terms during the third week of the month and take the provisional decision before year-end, the people said.

The European Commission's decision on the loan may not be made until well into next year, but EDF is optimistic an agreement will be reached with Brussels, the first source said.

The Commission did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

EDF is under pressure to launch the project before next year's presidential election, which could slow government decision-making and reshape French energy policy.

Marine Le Pen's far-right party, currently the frontrunner in polls, supports nuclear energy. However, Jean-Luc Melenchon, seen in polls reaching a second round but a long shot to win, is anti-nuclear.

To secure EU approval for the financing package, EDF has proposed auctioning 3,000 megawatts of output through long-term contracts to rival suppliers, ensuring competitors also benefit from the state-backed loan, the sources said.

The volume, equivalent to about 7% of EDF's annual output, would give competitors access to some of the electricity generated by the new plants rather than allowing EDF to reserve all of the output for its own customers or bilateral contracts.

($1 = 0.9108 euros)

(Reporting by Forrest Crellin; Editing by Dominique Patton and Joe Bavier)

data.title: American Resources Corporation and ReElement Technologies Selected as Part of Winning U.S.-Led Consortium for Kenya's Strategic Mrima Hill Critical Minerals Project
data.description:
FISHERS, IN / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / American Resources Corporation ( AREC ) ("American Resources") and ReElement Technologies Corporation ("ReElement"), a leading U.S. operator of advanced critical mineral refining and separation technologies in which American Resources ( AREC ) maintains a strategic minority ownership interest, today announced that the Frontier Minerals Consortium ("Frontier"), of which both companies are members, has been selected by the Government of Kenya as the successful bidder in the competitive international tender for the Mrima Hill Niobium, Rare Earth Elements and Other Minerals Development Project in Kwale County, Kenya.

The selection, announced by Kenya's Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs, represents a significant milestone in advancing one of the world's most strategically important undeveloped rare earth and niobium deposits. Frontier has been selected to enter exclusive negotiations toward a prospecting license, with subsequent activities subject to applicable regulatory approvals, community engagement and licensing requirements.

Frontier is partnered with American Resources ( AREC ), ReElement and Bunker Hill Silver Corp. ("Bunker Hill"), bringing together complementary expertise in mineral resource development, critical minerals supply chains and advanced refining technologies. The consortium's integrated approach is designed to support the development of a comprehensive mine-to-material value chain, emphasizing domestic processing and refining, local economic participation and long-term value creation in Kenya.

Through its Platform Orchestration model, American Resources ( AREC ) serves as a strategic supply-chain and commercial development partner, connecting mineral resource opportunities with advanced processing and refining capabilities, including those of ReElement, and downstream markets.

As part of its participation in the consortium, American Resources ( AREC ) expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier, subject to definitive agreements among the consortium partners. ReElement participates as the consortium's advanced refining technology partner, contributing its proprietary chromatography-based separation and purification capabilities, with the opportunity to generate refining-related revenues through future technology deployment, processing and commercial arrangements, subject to feasibility studies and definitive agreements.

The consortium is pursuing a capital-efficient development strategy that includes potential non-dilutive financing, government-supported funding and other strategic financing alternatives. Consistent with its Platform Orchestration model, American Resources ( AREC ) expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier while minimizing direct capital requirements and actively supporting the consortium through feasibility and development. This approach is designed to create long-term economic value for American Resources ( AREC ) and its shareholders while advancing Kenya's critical mineral development and in-country value-chain objectives, subject to definitive agreements.

A Differentiated Mine-to-Material Development Strategy

A central component of Frontier's proposal is the development of an integrated critical minerals value chain within Kenya, extending beyond traditional resource extraction and concentrate exports to include domestic mineral processing, advanced separation and refining, workforce development and downstream market integration.

The consortium's selection reflects a proposal designed to address Kenya's stated objectives for domestic mineral beneficiation, local economic participation, environmental stewardship and responsible resource development.

American Resources ( AREC ) contributes its international resource sourcing, feedstock aggregation, strategic partnerships and critical minerals supply-chain development capabilities. ReElement contributes its proprietary, patented chromatography-based separation and refining platform, designed to produce high-purity, specification-grade rare earth elements and other critical minerals through modular, scalable processing systems. Bunker Hill contributes mining, engineering, metallurgical processing and project development expertise, providing an integrated approach to evaluating and potentially developing the Mrima Hill resource.

Together, these capabilities are intended to support the development of a commercially sustainable supply chain that retains more economic value in Kenya while expanding access to strategically important critical minerals for U.S. and allied manufacturers.

Advanced U.S. Refining Technology Supporting Kenyan Value Creation

ReElement's chromatography-based technology represents a differentiated approach to critical mineral refining, utilizing water-based separation processes designed to reduce chemical consumption, energy requirements and environmental impacts compared with conventional solvent extraction methods.

Originally developed at Purdue University and licensed in 2021, the technology has since been advanced and commercialized through ReElement's proprietary research, engineering and intellectual property development. ReElement has validated separation and purification capabilities across 15 rare earth elements and additional critical minerals, achieving purities of up to 99.999% for select products.

The company commissioned its first commercial-scale chromatography columns for germanium production at the facility in August 2026 and continues to progressively scale its domestic refining capabilities.

ReElement's proposed role in the Mrima Hill project will focus on developing optimized commercial processing and refining flowsheets utilizing its proprietary chromatography-based technology. This approach is designed to support the phased deployment of modular refining infrastructure in Kenya, enabling the production of high-purity, value-added critical mineral products within the country, subject to project-specific technical, commercial and regulatory requirements. Beyond Mrima Hill, ReElement's participation is expected to create opportunities to evaluate additional critical mineral feedstocks throughout Kenya and the broader region, with the objective of leveraging potential shared refining infrastructure, enhancing capital efficiency and technology utilization, and supporting Kenya's emergence as a regional hub for advanced critical mineral refining.

This approach is intended to support the production of higher-value refined materials within Kenya rather than limiting the country's participation to the export of raw minerals or intermediate concentrates.

A Strategic Opportunity for Kenya and the United States

Mrima Hill contains historically identified rare earth and niobium mineralization, including elements important to permanent magnets, aerospace, advanced electronics and other strategic industries. Historical mineral resource estimates indicate significant mineralization; however, these estimates have not been verified as current mineral resources and will require further technical evaluation.

The project represents an opportunity to align Kenya's economic development and industrialization objectives with the United States' strategic interest in building diversified, secure, transparent and traceable critical mineral supply chains.

By supporting domestic processing and refining, the consortium's proposed development model seeks to create opportunities for Kenyan workers, technical professionals, suppliers and local communities while establishing additional sources of high-value critical materials for international manufacturers.

Mark C. Jensen, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Resources Corporation ( AREC ), commented: "This selection represents much more than an important milestone for the Frontier Minerals Consortium. It reflects a shared vision of how critical mineral resources can be developed to create lasting economic value for resource-rich countries while strengthening the industrial and national security interests of the United States and its allies.

"For too long, many resource-rich nations have participated primarily at the extraction stage of the global minerals supply chain, while much of the downstream processing, refining and economic value has been captured elsewhere. We believe the opportunity at Mrima Hill is to help change that model by bringing together world-class mining capabilities, advanced American refining technology and integrated supply-chain development.

"Our Platform Orchestration model is designed to create meaningful economic participation in strategic resource opportunities through partnerships and equity interests, while leveraging third-party capital and minimizing direct development expenditures. We believe this approach allows American Resources ( AREC ) to participate in globally significant projects while remaining focused on capital efficiency and the creation of long-term shareholder value.

"Importantly, this announcement is not the culmination of our efforts, but the beginning of a much broader opportunity. We look forward to working alongside the Government of Kenya, local communities and our consortium partners to advance a responsible, commercially sustainable development strategy that creates meaningful value for Kenya and strengthens critical mineral supply chains for the United States. We believe this collaborative approach can serve as a model for mutually beneficial partnerships in other resource-rich jurisdictions where we are actively developing relationships and opportunities."

Next Steps

Following the Government of Kenya's selection, Frontier intends to advance the required community engagement, regulatory and prospecting-license application processes in accordance with Kenyan law.

Subject to receipt of the necessary approvals, the consortium's proposed development program includes confirmation drilling, updated mineral resource evaluation, metallurgical test work, refining technology assessments, environmental and social studies, and preparation of a bankable feasibility study.

The feasibility process will focus on developing integrated mining, mineral processing and advanced refining flowsheets, leveraging ReElement's proprietary chromatography-based platform to support the production of high-purity, value-added critical minerals within Kenya. This approach is designed to establish a commercially viable, mine-to-material development model that maximizes in-country value-chain capture while supporting diversified critical mineral supply chains for the United States and its allies.

The consortium recognizes the environmental, cultural and social significance of Mrima Hill and intends to work with Kenyan authorities, local communities and other stakeholders to evaluate the project responsibly and in accordance with applicable requirements.

About American Resources Corporation ( AREC )

American Resources Corporation ( AREC ) operates a diversified critical materials platform through its Platform Orchestration strategy, which coordinates complementary capabilities across commercial feedstock origination, resource sourcing, industrial processing and advanced refining partnerships. This capital-efficient approach enables the Company to align resources, technologies and commercial relationships to evolving customer requirements and national priorities while strengthening U.S. and allied critical mineral supply chains.

The Company's operating platforms span conventional and unconventional resource sourcing, feedstock aggregation, recycling, processing and conditioning, complemented by its strategic ownership interest in ReElement Technologies Corporation, a leading U.S. advanced materials transformation and refining company. Through these complementary capabilities and strategic relationships, American Resources ( AREC ) seeks to connect diverse feedstock sources with advanced processing and refining solutions, enabling greater value chain capture and supporting growing commercial, industrial and defense-sector demand.

American Resources' ( AREC ) modular, asset-light business model emphasizes disciplined capital allocation, scalable operations and strategic partnerships. By coordinating specialized capabilities across the critical materials value chain without requiring traditional vertical integration, the Company seeks to expand commercial opportunities and support resilient, economically sustainable supply chains serving infrastructure, defense, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, energy and electrification markets.

For more information, visit americanresourcescorp.com or connect with the Company on Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn.

About ReElement Technologies Corporation

ReElement Technologies Corporation, a strategic portfolio holding of American Resources Corporation ( AREC ) , is a leading U.S. developer and operator of advanced materials transformation and refining technologies. Its modular, refining-first platform utilizes proprietary, patented chromatography-based separation and purification technology to transform diverse feedstocks - including primary mineral concentrates, recycled materials, industrial byproducts and other unconventional sources - into high-purity, specification-grade critical materials. ReElement's flexible technology enables the co-location of advanced refining capabilities closer to feedstock sources and downstream customers, supporting greater value chain capture while reducing chemical consumption and environmental impact. The Company supports secure, resilient U.S. and allied supply chains serving defense, aerospace, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, permanent magnets, energy and battery technologies.

By Anna Szymanski

LONDON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - From the Editor

This should have been a fantastic week for AI bulls: Nvidia's ( NVDA ) earnings were stellar, and Anthropic stormed the public markets with a blockbuster $81 billion IPO. But global equities have had a tough few days, with Asian stocks recording their worst week since 2020. The fallout from the Jensen Huang scandal continued with tighter US curbs on chip sales to China and news of more investigations, while fears of aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes also rattled investors.

Perhaps the hype surrounding the Anthropic IPO should be seen as a warning sign that the four-year-old bull market is getting stretched.

Anthropic's IPO was the one thing - besides perhaps the long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI - that could kick Nvidia out of the spotlight for at least a few hours. The artificial intelligence leader debuted on the Nasdaq on Thursday. It initially saw its share price climb as high as $115, up more than 38% from the offering price, before giving back a large chunk of that. While it still ended the day with a 17% rise, seeing its fully diluted valuation soar past $2 trillion, the share price has fallen further in premarket trading on Friday.

While there are plenty of reasons to be optimistic about Anthropic, it is coming to market at a challenging moment for the AI narrative, and concerns about the sustainability of its business model remain.

AI jitters weren't helped on Friday after a report by Hunterbrook Media suggested chip giant AMD's ties with Chinese entities could attract greater US regulatory scrutiny. Hunterbrook is shorting the firm. An AMD spokesman said, "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships."

All these tech worries hit Asian markets hard this week. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan tumbled 8.5%, the biggest weekly loss since March 2020.

This latest round of AI anxiety was supercharged last week by the dramatic ousting of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The erstwhile chief executive said on Monday that he "would be honored" to return to the company, a sentiment supported by many Silicon Valley leaders and even US President Donald Trump. However, the Nvidia board disagreed and said it has no plans to bring back the founder.

The longtime AI darling has shed an eye-popping $2 trillion in market cap in about six weeks, and the US Securities and Exchange Commission is now investigating the chipmaker, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Given this dramatic backdrop, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) earnings release on Tuesday seemed like a bit of a sideshow. The chipmaker beat revenue estimates for the 17th consecutive time, with third-quarter sales more than doubling to $115.84 billion. It also bumped up its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75% year-on-year. However, interim CEO Colette Kress was obviously unable to answer the questions that really matter to investors, namely who will succeed Huang in the long term and what is happening with the external investigations.

Likely in response to the Nvidia scandal, the Trump administration said on Monday that it would further limit China's access to advanced AI chips, including by restricting shipments via Southeast Asian countries that are often viewed as conduits to China. China's Commerce Ministry said Beijing would take countermeasures if the ‌US ⁠imposed the new rule.

One might have expected this to make for some awkwardness when Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping alongside the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Thursday for a trilateral meeting that also included Russian President Vladimir Putin. While the Chinese and Russian leaders did pledge on Wednesday to stand up against trade "protectionism," clearly a dig at the US, the actual meeting mostly featured warm smiles and handshakes.

This supposedly "high-stakes" discussion didn't produce any real breakthroughs. The three leaders put out a "peace declaration" on Thursday reaffirming that a nuclear war should never be fought, while also pledging to advance United Nations reforms, increase supplies of refined petroleum products, and uphold state officials' immunity in international courts.

One party was noticeably absent from the meeting: Europe. Of course, the European Union isn't part of APEC, but given the matters under discussion - including energy security, nuclear proliferation and the ongoing conflicts - it was noteworthy that Europe was left out. It's another reminder of Europe's inability to turn its economic heft into geopolitical power.

Nevertheless, the EU is reaching out to a trading partner closer to home this week. The UK and EU are holding a summit on Friday to focus on cooperation in trade, energy and mobility. This will be UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's first chance to show how serious he is about strengthening the relationship. He has previously stated that he would like to see Brexit reversed in his lifetime. He's 56.

Heading back to the US, the drumbeat for Fed tightening picked up this week. Fed minutes from the October meeting showed that most policymakers believed additional interest rate hikes would be necessary to return inflation to the central bank's 2% target, with some even considering a 50-basis-point rise.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller reinforced that on Wednesday, saying the Fed needed to get "aggressive" and shock people to ensure that today's 3% inflation rate would not become entrenched. This came after St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem on Tuesday said "several" hikes would likely be needed.

Meanwhile, US October retail sales came in higher than expected, rising 0.2% after an unrevised 0.8% surge in September. Import prices also rose more than expected, reinforcing the hot inflation reports released last week, as elevated energy prices crept into other goods and services.

However, oil prices are on track for another weekly decline. Crude was pulled in opposite directions this week by expectations for a near-term glut and continued attacks in the Middle East. Brent crude was holding above $90 a barrel on Friday morning.

data.title: Dominion Dynamics announces a Canadian consortium to develop Scout, Canada's first Autonomous Collaborative Platform
data.description:
Led by Dominion, 12 companies will form a Canadian-centred supply chain to advance autonomous aerospace in Canada

OTTAWA, ON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dominion Dynamics has brought together an initial group of Canadian companies to support Dominion Scout, an Autonomous Collaborative Platform (ACP) developed to meet Canada's defence needs and supply allied markets. Twelve companies have signed on to contribute technology, capabilities and operational expertise to Canada's first ACP, also known as a collaborative combat aircraft.

"The next generation of military aircraft will evolve at the speed of software. Canada has a chance to build that generation here," said Eliot Pence, founder and CEO of Dominion Dynamics. "That's why we're bringing Canadian aerospace companies together around Scout. We want to give Canada's Air Force a capability it can keep adapting at home and give Canadian companies a stake in an industry the rest of the world is racing to build."

The first round of development partners includes RTX's Pratt & Whitney Canada, Telesat, Thales Canada, Top Aces, ITPS Canada, PV Labs, SRC Can, Altitude Aerospace, Groupe DCM, HSB Solutions, North Aircraft Industries, and RAMPF Composite Solutions.

The Canadian consortium brings together expertise in aircraft structures and composites, landing gear, avionics and flight controls, engines, sensors and secure communications. Its capabilities also offer flight testing, training, maintenance and long-term fleet management.

Anchoring Scout's supply chain around Canadian suppliers puts domestic expertise at the centre of Scout's development, connects domestic suppliers to a rapidly growing defence market, and makes the thousands of jobs in these sectors more resilient. Specialized suppliers from NATO countries will also complement the Canadian industrial base.

"We're developing Scout with homegrown talent who know how to build aircraft, test them and keep them flying. Their expertise is shaping Scout's design from day one," said Benoit Breault, Senior Vice President of Aerospace Engineering at Dominion Dynamics. "Canadian capability is at the heart of Scout and its supply chain."

Scout is being designed for long distances, extreme cold and limited infrastructure in the Arctic. The aircraft is intended to operate alongside crewed fighter jets and receive tasking from airborne or ground-based command systems.

About Dominion Dynamics
Dominion Dynamics is an Ottawa-based defence technology company developing autonomy, sensing, communications and command and control systems for Canada and its allies. Founded in 2025, Dominion is building Scout, Canada's first Autonomous Collaborative Platform, and has deployed its AuraNet platform with the Canadian Armed Forces in the High Arctic. Learn more at defendthedominion.com.

data.title: GE Aerospace Recommends Shareholders Reject “Mini-Tender” Offer by Potemkin Limited
data.description:
CINCINNATI, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- GE Aerospace (NYSE: GE) received notice of an unsolicited "mini-tender" offer by Potemkin Limited (Potemkin) to purchase up to 10,000 shares of GE Aerospace common stock, which represents less than 0.001% of the shares outstanding, at a price of $186.00 per share in cash. Potemkin’s offer price is 34.88% less than the $285.64 closing price per share of GE Aerospace’s common stock on October 23, 2026, the last trading day before the mini-tender offer commenced and is 41.67% less than the $318.88 closing price per share of GE Aerospace’s common stock on November 19, 2026, the day prior to this press release.

GE Aerospace does not endorse Potemkin’s unsolicited mini-tender offer and recommends that GE Aerospace shareholders do not tender their shares in the offer because the offer is at a price significantly below the current market price for GE Aerospace’s shares.

Shareholders should obtain current market quotations for their shares, consult with their broker or financial advisor, and exercise caution with respect to Potemkin’s mini-tender offer. GE Aerospace recommends that shareholders who have not responded to Potemkin’s offer take no action. Shareholders who have already tendered their shares may withdraw them according to Potemkin’s offering documents.

Mini-tender offers seek to acquire less than five percent of a company's outstanding shares. Consequently, they can avoid many disclosure and procedural requirements of U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rules that apply to offers for more than five percent of a company's outstanding shares.

The SEC has cautioned investors about mini-tender offers, stating that mini-tender offers “have been increasingly used to catch investors off guard,” and that investors “may end up selling their securities at below-market prices.” The SEC's guidance to investors on mini-tender offers is available at https://www.sec.gov/reportspubs/investor-publications/investorpubsminitendhtm.html.

GE Aerospace encourages brokers and dealers, as well as other market participants, to review the SEC's letter regarding broker-dealer mini-tender offer dissemination and disclosure available at https://www.sec.gov/divisions/marketreg/minitenders/sia072401.htm.

GE Aerospace requests that a copy of this press release be included with all distributions of materials relating to Potemkin’s mini-tender offer for shares of GE Aerospace's common stock.
